title: Introduce FlashMosaic attention kernel with fused rope/rotary execution path
author: Priya Malhotra
description:
Motivation: reduce attention kernel overhead and memory footprint for long-context workloads (>=512 tokens) by combining a multi-granular tiling strategy with a fused rotary/rope micro-op path and light-weight KV hotset hints. FlashMosaic is a new kernel variant that: 1) applies adaptive block tiling (mosaic tiles) to better utilize shared memory across variable head sizes, 2) fuses rotary/rope position transformations into the Q/K compute path to avoid an extra memory pass, and 3) exposes a small KV hotset hint to the scheduler to prefer resident KV shards for streaming/batched sequences. This PR implements the kernel, integrates it into the kernel selection layer, and adds microbenchmarks + tests.

What changed (summary): added a new CUDA kernel implementation (flashmosaic) with C++ wrappers and a CPU fallback; extended the kernel selector to emit a FlashMosaic path when heuristics match (seq_len >= 256, head_dim % 32 == 0, GPU L2 >= 6MB); introduced a fused rope/rotary micro-op that is applied in-register during Q/K compute to eliminate a separate transpose + mul pass; added a KV hotset hint API to runtime and a scheduler heuristic that pins frequently accessed KV shards to resident pools when memory pressure allows; added microbenchmarks (runtime/bench/bench_flashmosaic.py), unit tests, and documentation snippets in docs/perf/.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel implementation (CUDA + wrappers)
- [x] Kernel selector / fallback logic
- [x] Unit tests for numerical parity vs existing flash variant
- [x] Microbenchmarks and CI performance gate
- [x] Documentation of heuristic knobs and runtime flags
- [x] Backwards-compatible CPU/GPU fallback

Performance highlights (internal bench):
- Up to +18% throughput at seq_len=1024, batch=8, model=7B on A100 GPUs (fp16)
- Median token latency decrease of ~9% for streaming small-batch workloads due to fused rotary path
- L2 load reduction measured in microbench: ~12% fewer global loads for fused rotary case
- KV hotset hint produced a 6-10% tail-latency improvement for bursty interactive workloads in our canary runs

Compatibility and safety: the kernel exposes a conservative selector; unsupported shapes fall back to the mature FlashBridge path. Numerical parity tests run across a matrix of head_dim ∈ {32,64,128}, seq_len ∈ {64,256,1024} and show max relative error < 1e-6 in fp16 accumulation mode. A runtime flag REDWOOD_ENABLE_FLASHMOSAIC (default on) is provided so operators can toggle at runtime.

Notes on design tradeoffs: fusing rotary removes a memory pass but increases register pressure. The mosaic tiling prefers larger shared-memory allocations which can reduce occupancy on older GPUs; selector heuristics keep this limited to GPUs with sufficient SM/shared resources. KV hotset hints are advisory and will not cause eviction anomalies; they are additive metadata passed to the scheduler and respected when memory headroom exists.

Related work: conceptually similar to earlier Flash variants but differs by the mosaic tiling pattern and in-register fused rotary. See ENG-9123 for design doc and perf traces.
